name: The Skinburn Flash (Augmentation Protest Mob)
description: A recurring protest phenomenon in which thousands of augmented citizens simultaneously activate visible chrome or subdermal lighting in public spaces, creating synchronized waves of bioluminescence and exposed metalwork as a direct challenge to Corponation policies that tax visible augmentation in Tier 3-4 commercial zones. Originating from a single spontaneous event outside the Halverson-Osei Civic Tower in 2211, the flash has since been coordinated through encrypted BCI mesh-pulses distributed by the anonymous collective known as Open Seam. The displays last exactly four minutes — the duration of the original 2211 protest before corp-sec dispersal — and have occurred in seventeen documented locations across M88.
cultural_impact: The Skinburn Flash has forced three separate corponation PR campaigns addressing augmentation taxation, and the sight of chrome lighting up a transit hub or shopping arcade has become an immediately recognizable symbol of tech-labor solidarity across M88's working tiers.
story_hooks: A corp-sec analyst realizes the BCI mesh-pulses contain a secondary layer of encrypted data being transmitted during each flash — someone is using the protest as cover for a massive data heist.
A player character is caught in a Skinburn Flash and accidentally activates augmentation they didn't know they had, suggesting someone installed something in them without consent.

Open Seam reaches out to recruit a fixer to protect the next flash from a rumored corp-sec crackdown — but the contact is a synthetic who claims to be one of the original 2211 protesters, which should be impossible.
